scope: Theorem 4.1 (Modular checksum estimator) of the manuscript “Subset Sum in Time $`O(2^{0.49n})`$” (preprints/Subset-Sum-in-Time-2-power-0-49n-October-4-2026/subset-sum.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 138 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 69f9398e325a2628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a constant d > 0. There is a uniform randomized procedure with the following guarantee for all sufficiently large n. Its inputs are an integer P with | log P − ηn| ≤ 2, arbitrary residues b1, . . . , bn modulo P, and a list T of at most nd target residues. It draws and retains independent uniform phases ϕ1, . . . , ϕn and either reports failure or returns estimates ˆ︁ Vρ for all ρ ∈ T . With probability 1 − o(1) it does not fail and |ˆ︁ Vρ − Vρ| ≤ 1 8 for every ρ ∈ T . The o(1) is uniform in P, the input residues, and the target list. On every random execution the procedure takes at most 2(τ+20ϵ)n+O( √ n) poly(n + |T |) (4.2) word operations. No primality assumption on P is needed.
